brief: Turn your three decisions from lesson 7 into records.
do: Write each decision as an ADR with Title, Status, Context, Decision and Consequences.
Give every record a sequential number and link it to the scenarios it serves.
In each Consequences section include at least one negative and one neutral effect.
Add a revisit trigger to each record, and list the three in a decision log table for arc42 section 9.
done: Evidence: Three ADRs, each linked to scenarios, and the section 9 decision log.
experienced: Apply it to a real system your team runs, with real numbers, real owners and real dates.
example:
### ADR-003: Queue offline orders on the phone
**Status:** accepted
**Context:** Q2 requires orders without a connection; vendors have weak data; one operations person.
**Decision:** We will store orders in a local queue and replay them on reconnect.
**Consequences:** (+) meets Q2. (+) no conflict rules, orders are append-only. (−) no offline editing. (neutral) server needs a duplicate check.
**Serves:** Q2, Q5. **Revisit:** offline edits requested in over 10% of tickets.
